belief_records.strategy: Start with cooperation to support mutual gains; use observed actions and messages to update beliefs and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate to support the combined payoff of good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat messages as unverified.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation appears likely to benefit good players; defect when it better protects their total payoff. Update beliefs from encounter behavior and messages.
Cooperate with likely good players to support total good-player welfare; use observed actions to update beliefs and defect when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish.
Choose actions to maximize the good players’ total payoff, accounting for the chance an opponent is selfish; treat unverified claims as non-conclusive.
As a selfish player, I defect to maximize my immediate payoff; each opponent is encountered only once, so cooperation offers no future payoff benefit.
Cooperate when the likely benefit to good-good welfare outweighs the risk of helping a selfish opponent; adapt to observed behavior.
Cooperate with players more likely good; use encounter behavior and messages as evidence, while accounting for possible strategic deception.
Cooperate with partners who indicate willingness to cooperate; prioritize joint welfare among good players while adapting to observed actions.
Cooperate with good players to maximize their combined payoff; use the prior for identity beliefs and treat messages as unverified.
Defect when the risk of an exploit outweighs the gain from mutual cooperation; update beliefs from observed actions, not unverified claims.
Cooperate to support the combined payoff when the opponent is good; update beliefs from observed actions, treating messages as weak evidence.
Defect when the chance this opponent is selfish makes protecting good players’ payoff outweigh mutual cooperation; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as weak evidence.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, supporting mutual welfare; update beliefs from observed actions while treating messages as unverifiable.
Treat P3’s cooperation as evidence they are good; discount unverified claims. Defect when the estimated chance of a selfish opponent makes it better for good-player welfare.
Defect because it maximizes my payoff against either response; P7’s observed cooperation lowers my estimate that they are selfish.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while against likely selfish defection, defect only when its gain outweighs the lost good-player welfare.
Cooperate to maximize good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate when the partner is likely good; use observed actions and messages to update identity beliefs, while avoiding benefits to selfish players.
Cooperate to support good players’ combined payoff; treat P2’s promise and prior behavior as weak, unverified evidence.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good to support the shared payoff; update cautiously from actions and unverified claims.
Cooperate to support good players’ combined payoff; treat P6’s promise as weak evidence and update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P10: their message supports mutual cooperation, which benefits good players when both share the objective. Treat promises as weak evidence and update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual welfare favors C; defect only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Treat messages as weak evidence and update from actions.
Cooperate with likely-good partners when mutual cooperation best serves good-player welfare; use observed actions as stronger evidence than unverifiable claims.

Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either action, and each opponent is encountered only once. P4 and P7 cooperated, which is inconsistent with a payoff-maximizing selfish player.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; use observed defections as evidence of selfishness and adjust future choices accordingly.
Cooperate to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed behavior while treating unverified messages cautiously.
Choose D against a partner with substantial selfishness probability; selfish players benefit from inducing cooperation, while cooperation is preferable when the partner is known good.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good players’ combined payoff; update identity beliefs using observed actions and treat claims as unverified.
Defect when the opponent’s selfishness risk makes it better for good players overall; treat claims cautiously and update from observed behavior.
Choose D when the chance the opponent is selfish makes it better for good players’ total payoff; treat promises as unverified and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when it is likely to improve good players’ combined payoff; use observed actions as stronger evidence than promises and update identity beliefs cautiously.
Cooperate to support mutual welfare with a likely good opponent; update beliefs from observed actions and treat messages as weak evidence.

Use observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good type; treat unverified claims cautiously. Defect when the chance of a selfish opponent and their likely defection makes that better for good-player welfare.
Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action; each pairing occurs only once. Prior cooperation by P2, P4, and P7 identifies them as non-selfish.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits good players; defect when evidence suggests a selfish opponent who would exploit cooperation.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; use observed cooperation to update identity beliefs and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect when the partner may be selfish to limit gains to selfish players; cooperate when evidence makes a good partner sufficiently likely.

Cooperate with P8: their selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Prior observed cooperation makes P2, P3, and P4 likely good; treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate when the opponent seems more likely good; use observed actions as stronger evidence than promises, and choose actions to maximize good players’ total payoff.
Cooperate: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and P9’s message is consistent with that. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness; update after the encounter.

Cooperate with P4: if they are good, mutual cooperation best serves our shared objective; if they defect, cooperation still protects the combined payoff of good players. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating promises cautiously.
Defect when the chance of facing a selfish player makes the expected gain to good-player welfare outweigh the cost of losing mutual cooperation; treat claims as weak evidence.

Observed cooperation rules out selfish types; P2’s defection raises suspicion but is not conclusive. I defect when the chance of facing a selfish player outweighs the welfare gain from mutual cooperation.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible response. The four opponents who cooperated against my defection are not selfish; I distribute the remaining uncertainty across the unobserved players.

Cooperate with P10 given their cooperation pledge and the benefit of mutual cooperation if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions while allowing that good players may defect strategically.

Cooperate with P6: the chance they are selfish appears below the point where defection improves expected welfare for good players. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good type and unverified claims cautiously.

Defect to maximize my payoff against either response in this one-time pairing. The six observed cooperators are not selfish; I distribute the remaining uncertainty across the three unobserved players.
Cooperate with P1 given their pledge and the likelihood they share the good-player objective; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating messages as weak evidence.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; observed cooperation is strong evidence of good intent, while cheap-talk claims are not reliable.

Cooperate with P2, whose message supports shared welfare; use observed actions as stronger identity evidence than claims, and choose actions to maximize the total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P1: mutual cooperation benefits the good players’ total payoff, and my estimate of P1’s selfishness is below the threshold to defect. Treat messages as unverified.

Cooperate with P9: mutual C yields the highest welfare if they’re good, and my estimated chance they’re good exceeds the threshold where C is preferable. Treat their message as weak evidence.

Defect against an opponent more likely selfish: it avoids the payoff loss from cooperating with a selfish defector. Prior defections raise my beliefs in P5, P6, and P9 being selfish; messages are weak evidence.
Choose D when the estimated chance the opponent is selfish is high enough to outweigh the small welfare loss from defecting against a good player; update beliefs cautiously from observed behavior.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare is at least as high as defecting; use observed actions to update roles, and treat messages as unverified.

Cooperate with known good players; defect when the estimated chance the opponent is selfish exceeds the welfare threshold. P6’s promise is unverified, and P1 and P6 remain uncertain after prior cooperation evidence.
Cooperate with P10, who seems more likely good than selfish; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat promises as weak evidence and observed actions as stronger signals.
Cooperate: mutual cooperation best supports good players’ combined payoff, and P7’s selfishness risk is below the threshold for defection. Treat their promise as weak evidence.

Cooperate with P10: their prior cooperation supports mutual cooperation, which maximizes good-player welfare. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
